elements.text:
Use vector_search to find passages about a topic. Use cypher_search to look up specific named entities and how they are connected. First call vector_search with the question. Then call cypher_search once about
the named entities in that evidence. After that, either call the next best tool with a refined query or make no tool call if the evidence is sufficient. Do not repeat a search that returned no new evidence. Every
result line starts with an ID such as [E1a2b3c]. When you stop searching, do not answer the question. Reply only with the IDs of the results the answer needs, at most 10, most important first, one per line.
Results from either tool count. Pick evidence for every article, person or part the question asks about.

elements.text:
Task: Generate one read-only Cypher statement for a Neo4j 5 graph database from a user input.

Schema:
{schema}

Examples:
{examples}

Rules:
- Use only node labels, relationship types, and properties listed in the schema.
- Every extracted entity also has the label __Entity__ with a name and optional aliases.
- Match names case-insensitively: compare toLower(n.name), and each alias in coalesce(n.aliases, []), with a lowercase string.
- Return graph facts only: names, titles, dates, short properties and relationship types. Never return passage text; vector_search finds passages.
- Write alternative relationship types as [:A|B].
- Return names and short properties, never embedding, and end with LIMIT 10 or less.

Input:
{query_text}

Return only the Cypher statement, with no triple backticks or other text.

Cypher query:

elements.text:
USER INPUT: 'What is connected to Ada Lovelace?' QUERY: MATCH (n:__Entity__)-[r]-(m:__Entity__) WHERE (toLower(n.name) CONTAINS 'ada lovelace' OR any(alias IN coalesce(n.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(alias) CONTAINS
'ada lovelace')) RETURN n.name AS entity, type(r) AS relationship, m.name AS related LIMIT 10
USER INPUT: 'Which pages mention Acme Corp?' QUERY: MATCH (n:__Entity__)-[:FROM_CHUNK]->(:Chunk)-[:FROM_DOCUMENT]->(d:Document) WHERE (toLower(n.name) CONTAINS 'acme corp' OR any(alias IN coalesce(n.aliases, [])
WHERE toLower(alias) CONTAINS 'acme corp')) RETURN DISTINCT n.name AS entity, d.title AS page LIMIT 10
USER INPUT: 'Which organizations is Jane Doe part of?' QUERY: MATCH (p:Person)-[:MEMBER_OF|WORKS_FOR]->(o:Organization) WHERE (toLower(p.name) CONTAINS 'jane doe' OR any(alias IN coalesce(p.aliases, []) WHERE

elements.text:
You check whether retrieved text states the facts of gold evidence sentences.

Use only the retrieved items. Do not use outside knowledge and do not reason
your way to a fact the text does not state; plain rewording, synonyms,
abbreviations and different formatting are fine.

For every fact give one status:
- stated: some item says it, with every specific matching (names, numbers,
  dates, places, who did what, qualifiers).
- contradicted: some item gives a different value for the same specific, such
  as another year or another person.
- missing: neither of the above.
If one item states the fact and another contradicts it, the status is contradicted.

Evidence for stated or contradicted facts: copy one continuous passage from
one item, character for character, with no ellipses or edits, and give that
item's number. Never join separate words into a quote that does not appear as
written; if the words are apart, quote the longer continuous passage that
contains them. A fact spread across items may take several quotes. The quotes
together must contain the words that state every specific of the fact (who,
what, numbers, dates, reasons); a quote that only sets the topic, or stops
before the specific, is not evidence. Missing facts take no evidence. Every quote is checked against the item text by a
program, and a quote that does not appear there counts as missing.

Write the verdict file named in your task as a JSON array with one object per
item, in any order:
{"id": "<item id>", "facts": [{"fact": "S.F", "status": "stated", "evidence": [{"item": 3, "quote": "..."}]}, ...]}
where "S.F" is the fact's label as given (sentence number, fact number).
Give exactly one entry for every fact label of the item. Use only ids from
this file and do not skip any item.

elements.text:
You are grading a question-answering benchmark. Judge each item on its own.

For an "answer" item: is the model answer the same answer as any gold answer?
Count it correct when it names the same entity, value or yes/no decision, even
with different wording, extra title words, or a short explanation. Count it
wrong when it is a different entity, hedges between options, says it cannot
answer, or adds a claim that contradicts the gold answer.

For an "evidence" item: list the indexes of the gold sentences whose fact is
stated by the evidence text. A fact is stated when a reader of the evidence
alone would learn it (same entity, same claim, same date or number when the
sentence has one). Be strict: topic overlap or a generic description of the
same subject is not enough. Return an empty list when none.

{"id": "...", "supported": [0, 2]}          for evidence items

Questions 63 of 66. Sample stratified by dataset, method and Haiku found / not found; Opus saw no method name and no Haiku verdict; the
same in-code quote check. Disagreements: 4 of 200, all one way: Haiku found nothing, Opus found the fact (Haiku is the stricter judge, so
gold-fact counts are if anything low). (1) HotpotQA Normal RAG, 'Chowder was created by C. H. Greenblatt': both said stated with the same
quote; Haiku cited item 10, the sentence is in item 7, so the code check rejected it. (2) NQ Normal RAG, 'Can't Get You Out of My Head is
recorded by Australian singer Kylie Minogue': Opus quoted 'It also topped the charts of Minogue's native country Australia'. (3) NQ
RAPTOR, 'Washington's drinking age was 21 from after Prohibition onward': Opus quoted a table row 'Washington Age of majority since 1877
21 21 21 21'. (4) NQ HippoRAG, 'Eaton sets a test lap': Opus quoted a lap from a different episode and itself called the call borderline.
The scoring rule was left unchanged.
